author: Methodius of Olympus
occasion: The surviving fragments praise martyrdom and reflect on the relation between human will and divine completion, probably to encourage Christians facing persecution.
argument: Methodius argues that martyrdom is so wonderful and prized that the Lord Jesus Christ himself, the Son of God, honored it by bearing witness to it, not considering equality with God a thing to be grasped, so that by this gift he might crown the man into whom he descended. He then states that every good action has its beginning in human will, but its completion rests with God. The fragments together present martyrdom as a divine gift that crowns human resolve, while insisting that the outcome of all good deeds belongs to God.
